title: A longer cold-water trial
hook: Would you repeat a longer trial if it ended more gently?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast accumulated discomfort with retrospective choice influenced by the ending.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast accumulated discomfort with retrospective choice influenced by the ending.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy trial has sixty seconds at intensity ten, then thirty at intensity five. What is its accumulated discomfort? Toy inputs A=[60, 10, 30, 5]; B=[60, 10, 0, 10].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[750, 7.5, 90], [600, 10, 60]]. Labels: Total discomfort, Peak-end score, Seconds.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The longer trial accumulates more discomfort but has a lower score under the explicit peak-end rule. The two metrics weight time differently. The toy separates those rules without diagnosing what any individual remembers or prefers.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses First seconds=60, First intensity=10, End seconds=0, End intensity=10. What is Total discomfort? Answer: 600.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses First seconds=60, First intensity=10, End seconds=0, End intensity=10. What is Total discomfort?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 600. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: After holding a hand in cold water for 60 seconds, and separately for 90 seconds ending slightly warmer, 69% chose to repeat the longer trial (Kahneman, Fredrickson, Schreiber & Redelmeier, 1993).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast accumulated discomfort with retrospective choice influenced by the ending.
